## SETTLED PREMISES (re-inlined; do not re-derive)

* **`fatal()` PRINTS AND RETURNS; only an explicit `exit(1)` ends the process** (`src/core/debugmsg.c`: `fatal()` has no
  early-out and no exit; the DATA arm is `fatal(...); exit(1);`).  The pass-2 brief failed to restate this, and deepseek's
  DO NOT SHIP rested on it -- the defect was the BRIEF's, not the seat's.
* The fix: the PORT arm refuses `idata >= 8` on the full `uint64_t`, keeps the previous selector, announces once per
  device (`warned_port`, `(once)` marker); the DATA arm's check and `exit(1)` are kept as a tripwire.  Unanimous in pass 1.

  48: struct fbctrl_data {
  49: 	struct vfb_data *vfb_data;
  50: 	int		current_port;
  51: 	int		port[DEV_FBCTRL_NPORTS];
  52: 	int		warned_port;	/* #549: the refused-selector announce */
  53: };
  54: 
  55: 
  56: /*
  57:  *  fbctrl_command():
  58:  *
  59:  *  Execute a framebuffer control command.
  60:  */
  61: static void fbctrl_command(struct cpu *cpu, struct fbctrl_data *d)
  62: {
  63: 	int cmd = d->port[DEV_FBCTRL_PORT_COMMAND];
  64: 	int x1, y1, i;
  65: 
  66: 	switch (cmd) {
  67: 
  68: 	case DEV_FBCTRL_COMMAND_NOP:
  69: 		break;
  70: 
  71: 	case DEV_FBCTRL_COMMAND_SET_RESOLUTION:
  72: 		/*
  73: 		 *  Change the framebuffer resolution to X1 x Y1 pixels.
  74: 		 */
  75: 		x1 = d->port[DEV_FBCTRL_PORT_X1];
  76: 		y1 = d->port[DEV_FBCTRL_PORT_Y1];
  77: 		debug("[ dev_fbctrl: changing resolution to %i,%i ]\n", x1, y1);
  78: 
  79: 		dev_fb_resize(d->vfb_data, x1, y1);
  80: 
  81: 		/*  Remember to invalidate all translations for anyone
  82: 		    who might have used the old framebuffer:  */
  83: 		for (i = 0; i < cpu->machine->ncpus; i++)
  84: 			cpu->machine->cpus[i]->invalidate_translation_caches(
  85: 			    cpu->machine->cpus[i], 0, INVALIDATE_ALL);
  86: 		break;
  87: 
  88: 	case DEV_FBCTRL_COMMAND_GET_RESOLUTION:
  89: 		if (cpu->machine->x11_md.in_use) {
  90: 			d->port[DEV_FBCTRL_PORT_X1] = d->vfb_data->xsize;
  91: 			d->port[DEV_FBCTRL_PORT_Y1] = d->vfb_data->ysize;
  92: 		} else {
  93: 			// When not using X11 output, return 0x0 size.
  94: 			d->port[DEV_FBCTRL_PORT_X1] = 0;
  95: 			d->port[DEV_FBCTRL_PORT_Y1] = 0;
  96: 		}
  97: 		break;
  98: 
  99: 	/*  TODO: Block copy and fill.  */
 100: 
 101: 	default:fatal("fbctrl_command: Unimplemented command %i.\n", cmd);
 102: 		exit(1);
 103: 	}
 104: }

 107: DEVICE_ACCESS(fbctrl)
 108: {
 109: 	struct fbctrl_data *d = (struct fbctrl_data *) extra;
 110: 	uint64_t idata = 0, odata = 0;
 111: 
 112: 	if (writeflag == MEM_WRITE)
 113: 	        idata = memory_readmax64(cpu, data, len);
 114: 
 115: 	switch (relative_addr) {
 116: 
 117: 	case DEV_FBCTRL_PORT:
 118: 		if (writeflag == MEM_READ)
 119: 			odata = d->current_port;
 120: 		else if (idata >= DEV_FBCTRL_NPORTS) {
 121: 			/*  #549: an out-of-range selector is REFUSED, and
 122: 			    current_port keeps its previous, always-valid value.
 123: 			    It used to be stored with only a warning, and the
 124: 			    next DATA access then ended the emulator in the
 125: 			    range check below.  Announced once per device.  */
 126: 			if (!d->warned_port) {
 127: 				fatal("[ fbctrl: port number 0x%llx is out of range; "
 128: 				    "the selector is unchanged (once) ]\n",
 129: 				    (unsigned long long) idata);
 130: 				d->warned_port = 1;
 131: 			}
 132: 		} else

 134: 		break;
 135: 
 136: 	case DEV_FBCTRL_DATA:
 137: 		/*  #549: unreachable while the PORT arm refuses; kept as a

 139: 		if (d->current_port < 0 || d->current_port

 159: 	}

   2: r"""#549 fbctrlportkill -- the DETECTOR for dev_fbctrl.c's port selector, on an UNMODIFIED `-E testmips`.
   3: 
   4: machine_test.c installs `fbctrl addr=0x12f00000` in testmips's own setup (and in default_test() for the other test
   5: machines).  Every access below is a real guest sb/sh/sw/sd/lw placed with `put w` and executed through real address decode
   6: and memory_rw -- stepped one instruction at a time, except session F, which free-runs to a breakpoint.  No machine or
   7: device is added to reach the site.  t0 = 0xffffffffb2f00000, kseg1 of DEV_FBCTRL_ADDRESS; PORT is +0x00, DATA +0x10.
   8: 
   9: THE DEFECT (HEAD before #549): the PORT arm STORED any selector with only a warning, and the DATA arm then called exit(1)
  10: on the stored int -- `sw 9` to PORT followed by any DATA access ended the emulator process.  #549 REFUSES a selector >= 8
  11: at the PORT arm (the previous, valid selector is kept) and announces the refusal once per device, `(once)`.
  12: 
  13: SESSIONS (each on a fresh emulator)
  14:   C  controls: PORT=5, DATA=0x2a, read both back (LIVENESS); X1=123, COMMAND=GET_RESOLUTION, read X1 (DEVICE SIGNATURE:
  15:      the model zeroes X1/Y1 without X11 -- RAM at +0x10 would read back 2, the last value written there, and a banked
  16:      register WITHOUT command execution would read 123); no `(once)` line may appear (nothing is refused).
  17:   A  accept: all EIGHT selectors, written at widths 1, 2, 4 and 8, each read back through PORT; ports 1-7 round-trip
  18:      a distinct DATA value (port 0 is COMMAND and is written only with NOP).
  19:   P  refusal, anchored to a previous selector: PORT=5 (DATA 0x2a), then nine out-of-range writes -- 9, 8, 16 (sw),
  20:      0x200000000, 0x100000003, all-ones (sd), all-ones (sw), 0xff (sb), 0x100 (sh) -- each PRECEDED by a fresh
  21:      PORT=5 and followed by a PORT read that must still say 5, so every row fails only on its own value; then
  22:      PORT=7 and a refused 9 must leave 7.  The `(once)` count must be exactly 1 right
  23:      after the FIRST refusal and still 1 after the last.

31-## 2. The four phases — every phase full-panel, flagship closes each
32-
33-| phase | file-reading seats | packet-fed seats | flagship closes with |
34-|---|---|---|---|
35-| 1 Assessment | independently characterize the bug — no shared packet (a shared brief = the author's errors, inherited) | attack the bug claim: prove it's not a bug / not yours / already fixed | a problem statement of record + an evidence grade |
36-| 2 Research | each proposes a fix WITH its grounding (spec section, datasheet, measured behavior — or an honest UNKNOWN) | attack the proposals: name what regresses under each | one chosen approach + named rejected alternatives (a do-not-relitigate list) |
37:| 3 Final review | per-diff review of the actual change + message truth check (does the commit message claim only what the diff does?) | attack the final diff's reasoning and its stated claims | the adjudication — last say |
38-| 4 Regression | verify test logs against pre-registered expectations; name the cross-consumer control up front | attack the test design: "what would this suite miss?" | pass/fail on the pre-registered predicate |
39-
40-Rules that bind the phases:
41-
42-- **Halt at every phase boundary.** The flagship's closure is presented to the owner as an explicit
43-  question, never a line in a status report, and the next phase dispatches only on their go.
44-- **Floor, not ceiling.** A phase closes when every seat has been heard at least once — but one
45-  round per seat is a floor. Follow-up rounds, targeted re-dispatches, and seat-vs-seat challenge
46:  through the coordinator are all allowed inside a phase.
47-- **Full-panel-or-pause.** If a seat is down mid-phase, that bug's phase pauses (it does not proceed
48-  short-handed); other bugs keep flowing. The pause is per-fix, never global.
49-- **Rejected bugs are still recorded.** "Not a bug" is a finding with a row, per-seat inputs, and a
50-  ruling — it feeds the do-not-relitigate list.
51-- **Round sizing:** substantive fix = 4 separate rounds; trivial fix = 2 dispatch rounds
52-  (assessment+research combined, review+regression combined) — same four columns recorded.
--
70-- Evidence ladder, on every claim: `CONFIRMED w/ source` > `MANUAL` (documented) > `BELIEVED`
71-  (inferred) > `UNKNOWN`. An honest UNKNOWN outranks a confident guess.
72-- Every ledger entry names a real file. An entry with no artifact behind it is not evidence.
73-- Verbatim seat outputs are banked under `evidence/<row>/<phase>/<seat>_<date>.md` — raw, not
74-  summarized. A new model joins by reading the row directory; nothing lives only in a chat context.
75-- A zero result is evidence only if the probe is proven capable of a non-zero result. Before
76:  trusting "no failures found", show the detector detecting a failure elsewhere.
77-- Co-occurrence is not attribution. A document that lists all your items does not count as a
78-  review of any one of them; only artifacts that name the item specifically do.
79-- Pre-register regression predicates before the run, so a pass cannot be redefined after.

56: <p><br>
57: <a name="intro"></a>
58: <h3>Introduction:</h3>
59: 
60: <p>GXemul can be started by entering machine settings directly on the command 
61: line, or by reading a configuration file (a "configuration script").
62: 
63: <p>Configuration files in GXemul are useful/necessary for three reasons:
64: 
65: <p><ol>
66:   <li>It can be difficult to remember long command lines with
67: 	lots of options.
68:   <li>Some settings cannot be fully controlled on the command line. They can
69: 	only be set using configuration files.
70:   <li>Complex setups of multiple machines, or complex network setups,
71: 	are not supported on the command line.
72: </ol>
73: 
74: <p>
75: Note that from a performance perspective, it is best to just have one
76: machine per configuration file, and run several GXemul instances concurrently
77: (with one machine per instance). The two advantages to having more than one
78: machine in a single configuration file are:
79: <ul>
80: 	<li>the network <tt>net ( )</tt> is trivially shared between the
81: 		specified machines, and
82: 	<li>breaking into the debugger will freeze all machines simultaneously.
83: </ul>
84: 
85: 
86: 
87: 
88: 
89: 
90: 
91: <p><br>
92: <a name="config"></a>
93: <h3>Configuration file syntax:</h3>
94: 
95: <p>Configuration files are simple text files.  I don't have time to write
96: down a formal syntax right now, so I hope that conveying the syntax
97: through an example is good enough:
98: 
99: <p>
100: <table border="0"><tr><td width="40">&nbsp;</td><td>
101: <pre>
102: <font color="#2020cf">!  This is an example configuration file for GXemul.
103: !  Anything following an exclamation mark (and also the exclamation
104: !  mark itself) is ignored.
105: !
106: !  Almost all settings are optional.</font>
107: 
108: <b>name(<font color="#ff003f">"my test emul"</font>)</b>	 <font color="#2020cf">!  Optional name of this emulation</font>
109:

114: 	<font color="#2020cf">!  local_port(12345)</font>
115: 	<font color="#2020cf">!  add_remote("localhost:12346")</font>

GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\crimewidthkill\fable_pass1_20260913.md-80-- **(a) CONTROL lane/label** -- restated, because the brief's sentence would send a round to the wrong line: the 4-byte arm is internally consistent (BE halves). The defect is the **switch**: `case CRIME_CONTROL` matches only the exact label `0x08` and tests raw `idata`, so a NetBSD-style 32-bit write at `0x00c` -- where bit 11 of a 64-bit BE register actually lives -- never reaches the reset/watchdog logic (`rows_*: sw CTL+0c 0x800 halted=no`, all builds). I rule against that majority-of-three on three grounds: the swap clause binds itself to *"the guard-field/body-field grep"*, which is about STATE fields that can disagree at different write sites, not instruction-encoding operands; the pass-11 bound names device-STATE lvalues, and `rd` is not one; and the swap reading makes floor membership depend on which constant the sibling dispatch happened to carry (`rd==0` only because `crn==0` dominates — had the arm been `crn 4`, `rd==4` would be floor and `rd==0` not). Grading by coincidence is the same vice as grading by cost. Codex's withdrawal is right. **Rule for the next pure deletion whose guarded body tests nothing: the floor is clause (b) verbatim reinstatement plus the dominating predicates' accept cell; every re-introduction keyed on a body-read operand the body does not test (`rd == k`, `field & bit`, `field == v`) is clause (e), disclosed BY CLASS in the CONTRACT; any row added for one is L1 construction — licensed because cheap, never graded floor because cheap.** Grade F1/F2 as L1 + (e) in the CHANGELOG. GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\fbctrlportkill_20260924\fable5_p1.md:6:**Top line — the one disposition-level change I require:** F2 says "Opus measured each row load-bearing." It did not. `opus5_p1b.md` measured **boundary, wide, announce** as sole catchers and stated plainly that the **negative (`sw -1`) and controls-`(once)` rows caught nothing it built**. More seriously, the panel's most-cited escape — an `int64_t idata` / `(int64_t)idata` compare — was **predicted by six seats and never compiled**: the built mutants are `e_int` = `(int)idata` (32-bit), not a 64-bit signed one, and the row that would kill it (`sd -1`, bit 63 set) is **absent from the measured `rows_probe.py`**. So F2's *direction* is right ("rows per enumerated edit") but its *evidence claim is overstated and its headline row is unmeasured*. This is L1 pre-ship construction and must be closed by a measured kill before the detector ships, per this project's own "a mutant that will not die / an accept row is discharged by a MEASURED KILL, not by prediction" rule. Everything else proceeds.

GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\fbctrlportkill_20260924\fable5_p1.md-8-**Ruling 1 (F1 — keep the DATA-arm `exit(1)`, or quiet-refuse?): KEEP it.** I read both precedents. `#521` (CHANGELOG) leaves an unreachable `default:` "deliberately in place as a tripwire for a later edit" — the direct precedent. Codex's dissent cites `sh4_val_first()` (`dev_sh4.c:1824-1841`), which I read: it *is* an unreachable bounds check that returns 0 silently. But its own comment says it silences **because "an unbounded key must not become an unbounded print"** — i.e. flood control for a helper called in a guest loop. The DATA guard is unreachable and non-looping, so that warrant does not transfer. Codex's stated reason — "a future upstream-check regression would restore process termination" — is *inverted*: that is the tripwire working, converting a re-opened PORT bug into a loud death rather than a silent OOB into `port[bad]`. Opus **measured** this: with `>` accepting 8, the kept guard fires loudly. Keep it, and disclose under clause (e) that it is unobservable on a correct build. (I keep codex's dissent as the second-strongest option; its idiom is real, its warrant backwards.)

So "no new oracle" holds only at the plumbing level, not the assertion level. No rule amendment is needed — state that the *semantic-class / one-fix-design* clause is what excludes it. kimi-sub's challenge does land on one point and F6 already honors it: the round **must not** claim "fbctrl can no longer kill the host." It closes the DATA-arm path only; the command default and offset default stay guest-reachable (opus walk: 4 `CMD-UNIMPL` + 52 `UNIMPL-ADDR` cells survive into death on the fix build). GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\fbdrainwire_20260924\opus5_p1.md-90-- **What I measured:** with the ceiling deleted, run at depth 2147487744, R2 prints `ok R2 no signed overflow … peak 2147483647 trough 1`.
GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\fbdrainwire_20260924\opus5_p1.md:91:- **Why:** the comparison runs before the increment and resets the counter to 1, so it fires at INT_MAX and no int-sized bound can overflow. Both are wrong records (L4); file them, and do not cite the ceiling deletion as a #442 regression.

GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\m88kexcdeliver\fable_p2.md-11-- Manual, pointer definitions `mc88100.txt:2097-2104`: "For sequential execution ... (FIP = NIP+4). ... Unconditional branch addresses are computed from the XIP plus the signed 26-bit word displacement (FIP = XIP + d26). Conditional branch addresses for the branch taken case are calculated as FIP=XIP+d16." Same from the instruction side, `:4207-4208` (bsr): "Operation: FIP <- XIP+D26x2; r1 <- NIP (+4 if .n option)". So while the branch is in XIP: NIP = branch+4 (the slot), FIP = target. One stage later, while the SLOT executes: NIP = target, FIP = target+4. A precise fault in the slot therefore leaves SXIP = slot, **SNIP = target|V, SFIP = target+4|V**.
GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\m88kexcdeliver\fable_p2.md-12-- Corroboration: `:8940-8947` lists the only three reasons SNIP.V is clear — the branch-related one is "the instruction pointed to by the SNIP followed a branch ... invalid if the .n option was not specified and the branch is taken" (NIP = branch+4 while XIP = branch); nothing annuls the instruction two after a taken `.n` branch, which the fork's model would require. `:8898-8902`: SFIP is "the instruction following the next instruction OR the target of a jump or branch" — the latter is the state while the BRANCH is in XIP (what an interrupt after a branch sees), not while the slot is. rte flow `:9023-9033`, `:9040-9050`: NIP <- SNIP, FIP <- SFIP; the SNIP instruction executes, then the SFIP one.
GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\m88kexcdeliver\fable_p2.md-13-- The fork (`cpu_m88k.c`, anchor `Perhaps something like this could work`): `SNIP = (pc+4)|V; SFIP = delay_target|V` — the previous stage's state, and upstream's own comment says it is a guess. The fork's sibling arm two lines up (anchor `vector == M88K_EXCEPTION_DATA_ACCESS` inside `if (cpu->delay_slot)`) already has the correct shape (`SNIP = delay_target|V; SFIP = SNIP+4`) — the in-tree precedent, exercised by OpenBSD on every page fault in a delay slot.
GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\m88kexcdeliver\fable_p2.md-14-- Guest-visible consequence via `X(rte)` (anchor `The NIP instruction should first be executed`): when SFIP != SNIP+4, rte executes the SNIP instruction and then jumps to SFIP. After a delivered slot fault: taken `br.n` with target != slot+4 -> executes slot+4 (an instruction the taken branch skipped) then the target; target = slot+4 (the probe's row) -> SNIP == SFIP -> executes the target TWICE; not-taken `bcnd.n` (`X(bb0_n)`: `delay_target = cpu->pc + 8`) -> SFIP == SNIP -> executes slot+4 twice. Observable whenever a handler returns to the context (OpenBSD signal handler + sigreturn; any kernel fixup).

GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\m88kexcdeliver\opus_p2.md-29-
GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\m88kexcdeliver\opus_p2.md:30:**(1) M_NOVBR — L2, floor breach, repair in-round.** `cr[VBR]` is a field the guarded body reads on the delivery path the seven added labels route through, so it is squarely inside the clause-(d) DEPENDS-ON closure, and dropping it is the canonical *keep the guard, null the repair* form: all seven `implemented = true` and all seven tail labels survive textually and the exception lands at the wrong address. **The probe never writes VBR** (`grep -i vbr` on the frozen probe: one docstring mention, no `stcr cr7`), so VBR is 0 in all twelve rows and `cr[VBR] + 8*vector` is arithmetically indistinguishable from `8*vector`. Guest effect: OpenBSD/mvme88k relocates its vector table, so every one of these seven exceptions would enter at the wrong address on the very guest the fix exists to serve. It is compounded by an **L4 wrong record in two places**: the fallback comment says *"DELIVERED (**VBR** + 8\*vector …)"*, and the probe's clause-(e) contract lists *"a wrong vector base"* among what it **catches** — M_VEC4 and M_VEC7 pin the *scaling*, nothing pins the *base register*.
GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\m88kexcdeliver\opus_p2.md-31-
GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\m88kexcdeliver\opus_p2.md-32-**(2) M_SFRZTRAP — L2, an empty joint cell that the manual makes load-bearing.** The delivery path's own code tests two lvalues: `if (cpu->cd.m88k.cr[M88K_CR_PSR] & M88K_PSR_SFRZ)` and `if (!is_trap)`. The body-tested partition is therefore {SFRZ clear, set} x {is_trap 0, 1}. The rows hold three cells — (clear,0) most rows, (clear,1) bounds/privtb/errortb, (set,0) the `error` row — and **(set,1) is empty**. It is not hypothetical: `_scratchpad/mc88100.txt:8633-8636` says *"When the MC88100 is in the exception processing state, it cannot process another exception **except for trap instructions**"*, and 6.10 at `:10613-10614` repeats it, so the `!is_trap` guard is architecture, not defensiveness. And the reachable instance is the guest's own syscall: OpenBSD issues syscalls as `tb0`/`tb1` naming 0x80/0x1c2, so under this mutant **a syscall made from a handler that has not yet re-enabled shadowing becomes a fatal ERROR exception at 0x50**.

GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\lunaabsentcpu\fable_p1.md:33:**F2. The corollary is MASK-DEPENDENT (glm UPHELD).** Kill iff the asserting line's bit is in the armed absent-slot mask AND `irqActive[k]` is clear. With `0xfc000000`, all six lines kill. With es438-D4's `0x84000100` (= 0x80000000 | 0x04000000 | 0x00000100: bits 31, 26, 8 — enumerated, bit 26 SET, the corrected sentence is right) only line 6 (clock, bit 31) and line 1 (bit 26) can; sio (30), le (29), scsi (28) cannot. GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\lunaabsentcpu\fable_p1.md-34-
GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\lunaabsentcpu\fable_p1.md-35-**F3. THE SIO LINE-5 ROUTE IS SYNCHRONOUS AND GUEST-DRIVABLE WHILE STEPPING (kimi UPHELD, verified).** Anchor `case OBIO_SIO + 4:` (cmd channel 0, 0x51000004): first write with `obio_sio_regno == 0` selects `regnr = idata & 7` (store 0x01 -> WR1); second write lands `d->obio_sio_wr[sio_devnr][regnr] = idata`; then `if (d->obio_sio_wr[sio_devnr][SCC_WR1] & SCC_WR1_TX_IE && !old_tx_enable) d->sio_tx_pending[sio_devnr] = 1;` -> `reassert_serial_interrupt(d)` -> `INTERRUPT_ASSERT(d->sio_irq)` -> `luna88k_interrupt_assert` (connected to `%s.luna88k.5`, `templ.line = 5`) -> `interrupt_status |= 1 << 30` -> `reassert_interrupts(d)`. `SCC_WR1_TX_IE` = 0x02 (`src/include/thirdparty/sccreg.h`). Two word stores, no host timer. **Disarm is also synchronous**: a cmd write of 0x28 (`SCC_RESET_TX_IP`) -> `sio_tx_pending = 0` -> `INTERRUPT_DEASSERT(d->sio_irq)` -> bit 30 cleared -> `reassert_interrupts` — which, under an ASSERT-only NULL check, is a DEASSERT of NULL: the disarm doubles as the M_NULLCHECK row. Session-order caveat: bit 30 stays pending machine-wide until disarmed, so place the arming after W1 or disarm at once, or the pre-fix session dies on an arming store instead of a SOFT store.

GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\pcc2widthkills\pass10_seats_20260904\fable\FINDINGS.md-30-
GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\pcc2widthkills\pass10_seats_20260904\fable\FINDINGS.md-31-2. *"arbitrary BOOLEAN COMBINATIONS are exponential → #392."* This half is **correct and important**, but over-shoots. The fix is not "forbid multi-lvalue cells" — it is to bound the enumeration to the partitions the **body itself tests** (a fixed, small product), not a free boolean algebra. And "single-operand is complete" leaks (see below), so the dissent's own escape hatch fails.
GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\pcc2widthkills\pass10_seats_20260904\fable\FINDINGS.md-32-
GXEMUL-SEC\regress\artifacts\pcc2widthkills\pass10_seats_20260904\fable\FINDINGS.md:33:3. *"row demand is PER ENUMERATED MUTANT → no row owed."* True rule, **wrong application.** The carrier: *"Rows are owed PER ENUMERATED MUTANT, never per refusing state; two states no enumerated mutant distinguishes collapse into one row."* Once point 1 falls, the conjunction **is** an enumerated (d) cell, distinguished from every existing row's state (no row holds both pending). So the per-mutant rule Opus cites **owes** the row. He wields a rule that supports the row to deny it.

The PORT arm in `GXEMUL-SEC/src/devices/dev_fbctrl.c` does refuse a full `uint64_t` `idata >= 8`, leaves `current_port` unchanged, latches `warned_port` once, and keeps the DATA `exit(1)`. ## 1. Device edits outside table 2 that stay 41/41

Table 2 already kills a bad compare, a bad store, and a bad latch in the PORT arm (`M_i64`, `M_u32`, `M_store`, `M_reset0`, `M_wide`, `M_acc4`, `M_noguard`, `M_static`). These are different sites. Each leaves every current row green. The row named is the one that looks like it should go red.

**1. Full 64-bit refuse, bit 63 only.** Replace the predicate with

```c
else if ((idata & ~(1ULL << 63)) >= DEV_FBCTRL_NPORTS) {
```

Arithmetic: a tested refuse stays a refuse because its low 63 bits are still `>= 8` (`8`, `9`, `16`, `0xff`, `0x100`, `0xffffffff`, `0x100000003`, `0x200000000`, and all-ones, whose low 63 bits are `2^63-1`). Accepts `0..7` have bit 63 clear. The eight values `2^63 + 0..7` take the accept arm. `current_port` is an `int`, so `2^63` stores as `0`. That is in range, so the DATA check does not exit, and a following DATA write with the selector at `0` enters `fbctrl_command()`. Row that stays green: `refuse all-ones (sd), PORT keeps 5`. This is the hole behind the header's "bit 63" claim. `M_i64` goes red on that same row because a signed compare rejects all-ones, which still has every other bit set.

**2. Previous selector, only the memset zero.** At the bottom of the refuse arm, after `d->warned_port = 1;`:

```c
if (!d->current_port)
    d->current_port = (int) idata;
```

`memset` leaves `current_port == 0` (`DEV_FBCTRL_PORT_COMMAND`). Sessions P and K store `5` or `7` before they refuse, so the `if` is false there. Session F is the power-on case: one `sw` of `9`, no PORT read, no DATA access (`PROG_F`, empty read list). The announce still matches and the breakpoint is still reached. Row that stays green: `refuse 9 (sw), PORT keeps 5`. The broken session's own row, `F refusal announced while free-running (fatal)`, also stays green. `M_reset0` is the always-store-`0` edit and is red on the keeps-5 rows. This one stores the bad selector only when the previous value is the reset `0`.

**3. Once per device, cleared from `fbctrl_command()`.** First line of that function:

```c
d->warned_port = 0;
```

Session C does call it (`PORT=0`, DATA `2` = `GET_RESOLUTION`) and then never refuses, so the clear is invisible. Session P's only DATA write is `0x2a` to port `5` (`DEV_FBCTRL_PORT_COLOR_R`), so `fbctrl_command()` does not run between the ten refusals. F never touches DATA. Row that stays green: `announce: still exactly 1 after ten refusals`. A command, then another bad selector, announces again.

**4. DATA check, field order.** In the DATA arm only, delete one character:

```c
if (d->current_port < 0 || d->current_port
    > DEV_FBCTRL_NPORTS) {
```

A correct PORT arm never stores `8`, so every DATA access in the probe still has a selector in `0..7` and the body of the check still does not run. Row that stays green: `K survives DATA after a refused PORT write`. Reading of the struct, not a compiled `offsetof`: the fields are pointer, `int current_port`, `int port[8]`, `int warned_port`, with no pack pragma. Those `int`s are adjacent on both LP64 and ILP32, so `&port[8] == &warned_port` and `&port[-1] == &current_port`. With `>` , a selector of `8` misses `exit(1)` and `d->port[8] = idata` writes the latch. Deleting only `d->current_port < 0 ||` is the same class of edit: a selector of `-1` misses the exit and the store hits `current_port`. `M_noguard` deletes the whole check. This leaves the check in the file and opens the one index that aliases the latch.

**5. PORT read / `odata`, widths above 4.** On the read arm:

```c
odata = (uint64_t) d->current_port | (1ULL << 32);
```

Reading of `memory_writemax64` (`src/core/memory.c`): it writes `len` low bytes. Reading of `cpu_mips_instr.c`: `lw` is size code 2, four bytes. Every PORT read in the probe is `lw`, so bits 32 and up never reach a register. Row that stays green: `C LIVENESS: PORT reads back 5` (got stays `0x5`). The probe boots `-M 64` and never emits `ld`. An `ld` returns `0x100000005`. `sdl`/`sdr` (`mips_unaligned_loadstore`) read eight bytes, merge, and write eight back, so that write sees a value `>= 8` and is refused.

**6. Widths the accept matrix never pairs.** Same predicate site:

```c
else if (idata >= DEV_FBCTRL_NPORTS || (len < 4 && idata == 0)) {
```

`ACC` writes selector `0` only with `sw` (`len == 4`). Session C's command select is also `sw` of `s0`. No `sb`/`sh` of `0` exists, so nothing announces and no accept row moves. Row that stays green: `accept selector 0 written by sw`. An `sb` of `0` is a legal selector and is refused.

## 3. Sentences the diff adds

**False. Gate comment and the new PORT comment in `dev_fbctrl.c`.** Both say a store of an out-of-range selector was stored with a warning and the next DATA access ended the emulator. The old arm did `d->current_port = idata` with `current_port` an `int` and `idata` a `uint64_t`, and the warning tested the full `idata`. The DATA exit tests the stored `int` (`< 0` or `>= 8`). On the LP64 host the WSL builds used, that conversion keeps the low 32 bits. `sd` of `0x200000000` stores `0`. `sd` of `0x100000003` stores `3`. Both are inside `0..7`, so the next DATA access does not exit. Those two values are in the probe's own refuse list. `sw` of `9` does exit. That is the case the probe header states, and that sentence is the true one: exit is on the stored `int`, and the example is `sw 9`.

**False for the code this diff commits. Probe NOT CLAIMED, the latch sentence.** `warned_port` is at `&port[8]` (same layout reading as finding 4). The DATA arm calls `exit(1)` before any `port[current_port]` use. A selector of `8` that a broken PORT arm stored hits that exit and does not write the latch. The write lands on the latch only when the check is also gone or its `>=` has become `>`, which is finding 4. The exit body is what a correct PORT arm makes unreachable. The check's condition still runs on every DATA access.

**True only for the signed all-ones case. Probe CATCHES, "bit 63".** `M_i64` is red on `refuse all-ones (sd)` because a signed compare sees `-1`. Finding 1 clears only bit 63, leaves that row green, and accepts `2^63`. The row observes "all 64 bits set", not bit 63.

**True only when the re-select store lands. Probe session P: "so every row fails only on its own value."** Reading of `table2/M_acclatch.raw`: accepts die after the first refusal, the later `PORT=5` stores do not land, and `refuse 9 (sw), PORT keeps 5` and `refuse 8 (sw), PORT keeps 5` are both `got=0x5`. The only red row is `refuse 9 after PORT=7, PORT keeps 7` (`got=0x5`). Those green keeps-5 rows are a selector that was already `5`.

**False. Probe NOT CLAIMED: "every machine installs ONE fbctrl".** Reading of `machine_test.c`: `default_test()` and `MACHINE_SETUP(testmips)` each call `device_add` of `fbctrl` once. `baremips` / `barearm` add none. `emul_parse.c` can `emul_add_machine` more than once, and `emul.c` runs every machine. The probe's `-E testmips` path has one (`emul_simple_init` requires `n_machines == 1`), so a process-global latch matches a per-device latch for these 41 rows. That is the measured case. A second test machine in one process is a second `fbctrl_data` and shares `M_static`'s latch.

1: #!/bin/bash
2: # GATE 16 -- MIPS instruction-combiner ("fold") witness (#388).
3: #
4: # What this protects
5: # -----------------
6: # The nine MIPS COMBINE sites install 34 fold-handler variants, and before #388
7: # NOTHING could witness one firing: most folds are architecturally transparent
8: # by construction, so any result-asserting row passes whether or not the fold
9: # fires -- the recorded vacuity mode. #388 added pull-only install/fire counters
10: # (cpu_mips.h) printed by tlbdump as a prefix-bound MFOLD block. This gate runs
11: # regress/mips_fold_probe.py, whose rows drive real fold loops free-running
12: # (never step -- combining gates on !single_step) with a breakpoint AFTER each
13: # sequence on a NON-ARMING instruction, and grades the counters as EQUALITIES
14: # derived from the read-ahead rule (a breakpoint anywhere disables read-ahead
15: # machine-wide, so fire == passes-1; the derivations live in the probe's rows).
16: #
17: # Non-vacuity: deleting the bne_samepage_nop replacement sub-arm (incl. its
18: # install++) in a scratch build flips exactly that fold to (0,0) and reddens
19: # its two rows while every other row stays green -- measured 2026-08-12
20: # (M388MUT_PASS), the per-variant attribution -J cannot give.

## 0. WHAT PASS 1 SETTLED (fable5_p1b.md, claude-fable-5-1; re-inlined so nobody re-derives it)

* **The fix:** the PORT arm REFUSES a selector >= 8 on the full 64-bit `idata`, keeps the previous (always-valid)
  selector, and announces the refusal once per device with the house `(once)` marker.  Unanimous across nine seats.
* **The DATA arm's range check and `exit(1)` are KEPT, unedited except for a comment**, as a tripwire: once PORT refuses
  it is unreachable, and it is what stands between a future broken PORT arm and `port[8]` (which, after this diff's
  struct change, is the `warned_port` latch).  Precedent: `#521` left an unreachable `default:` exit "deliberately ... as
  a tripwire".  Dissent (codex panel, pass 1): make it a quiet refusal -- ruled against on the arguments.
* **Out of scope and FILED, not taken:** `fbctrl_command()`'s `default:` (any command other than 0-2, including the
  documented but unimplemented FILL (3) / COPY (4)) and the access function's `default:` (any offset other than 0x00 /
  0x10).  Both still end the process.  The Opus seat MEASURED that keep-previous-from-reset routes "refused selector,
  then a DATA write of an unknown command" into the command default; the contract says so.  Dissent (kimi-sub): the
  command default meets the reopening rule -- ruled against: a different fix design (implement vs decline FILL/COPY).
* **The rung-3 witness is valid** (unmodified `-E testmips`, stepped real `sw`/`lw`, liveness + device-signature +
  disassembly controls, death AND diagnostic required).  On HEAD: `sw 9` to PORT then `lw` from DATA ends the process,
  exit status 1.

3. GUARD FIELD vs BODY FIELD
   Refusal guard reads: idata (uint64_t, from memory_readmax64 over len bytes), writeflag.
   Refusal body reads/writes: d->warned_port.  Accept body writes: d->current_port (from idata).
   DATA guard reads: d->current_port.  DATA body reads: d->port[d->current_port], d->current_port (== COMMAND test).
   Who else writes d->warned_port?  grep: only the refusal body (and DEVINIT's memset).  Who else writes
   d->current_port?  only the accept branch (and memset).  No shared bitfield; no third state of either field is
   reachable, so no disagreeing-state row is owed.  The operand the guard tests (idata) is the value the accept branch
   stores, so guard and store cannot disagree except through a mutant (enumerated below).

4. CHANNEL -- per row, the mutant(s) it is predicted to kill and the observable that differs (PREDICTIONS):
   refuse 9 (sw), PORT keeps 5        M_revert M_store M_clamp M_reset0 M_and5*  PORT reads 9 / 1 / 0 / 5&5=5*
       (* &=5 from 5 is invisible here -- that is why "refuse 9 after PORT=7" exists: 7&5 = 5)
   refuse 8 (sw)                       M_gt M_bit(8 has bit 3 -> refused: NOT killed here)    PORT reads 8
   refuse 16 (sw)                      M_bit (16 has neither bit 3 nor 32)                     PORT reads 16->current 16
   refuse 0x200000000 (sd)             M_mod33 (0x200000000 % 2^33 = 0 -> accepted as 0)       PORT reads 0
   refuse 0x100000003 (sd)             M_u32 M_i32 (truncate to 3)                             PORT reads 3
   refuse all-ones (sd)                M_i64 M_decl (negative -> accepted, stored -1)          PORT reads -1
   refuse all-ones (sw)                M_i32 ((int)0xffffffff = -1)                            PORT reads -1
   refuse 0xff (sb)                    M_wide (1-byte write skips the refusal)                 PORT reads 0xff
   refuse 0x100 (sh)                   M_wide                                                  PORT reads 0x100
   refuse 9 after PORT=7, keeps 7      M_and5                                                  PORT reads 5
   accept selector p (x8, widths 1/2/4/8)  M_rej2 (p=2) M_acc4 (p written by sb/sh/sd)         PORT reads previous
   port p round-trips DATA (x7)        M_rej2 M_acc4 (DATA lands in the previous port)         DATA reads other cell
   announce: exactly 1 after FIRST     M_latchinv (0) M_latchcnt (0) M_revert (0: WARNING text) (once) count
   announce: still 1 after ten         M_latch0 (10) M_perval (10: every value differs)        (once) count
   F refusal announced free-running    M_debug (debug() is silent while free-running)          (once) count 0
   C nothing refused, no (once) line   M_ann_any (announces on the accepted PORT=5)            (once) count 1
   K survives / DATA 0x2a / write 0x77 M_revert (HOST-DIED at the DATA read), M_store (same)  survival, DATA cells
   C/A/P/K disassembly, liveness, signature   controls: a harness or encoding fault, not a mutant.
   PREDICTED ESCAPES, DISCLOSED (clause e): M_static (process-global latch -- one device per machine), M_noguard (the
   DATA check deleted -- unreachable on a correct PORT arm).
   FLOOR: (a) HEAD fails (25/41, measured); (b) M_revert is HEAD's PORT arm verbatim at the one fixed site;
   (c) the gate pins FBCTRLP_RESULT=41/41, FBCTRLP_CONTROL=OK and FBCTRLP_DONE, so a null or truncated probe reds.

Rows are owed PER ENUMERATED MUTANT, never per state.  Mutant source: mutants549.py (23 mutants, find-text-must-match).

That supports disclosing `idata != 10`; merely invoking the size of the input space would not establish the disposition. The unreachable DATA-check changes and output-equivalent `printf` substitution also need no new row here.
